[RL-0013] Keep each script short and direct, about 120 lines or fewer: loop over columns instead of repeating blocks, no commented-out alternatives, no long docstrings, no restating of these instructions. A complete short script is better than an elaborate one that is cut off.
[RL-0014] When repairing, read the error type and message in the diagnostics first and change the smallest part of the script that causes it; keep the approach, inputs and outputs. A message about specifying columns with strings on non-dataframes means an array reached a name-based transformer (see RL-0009 and RL-0011). A KeyError on a JSON key means a guessed structure; use the keys the file has. Messages starting with 'MLCA:' state an engine rule; comply, do not work around it.

Every fit_record call still uses all training rows; compute expensive diagnostics that fit nothing on a fixed-seed subsample of at most 10000 rows and print its size.
[RL-0017] For binary roc_auc, align the positive probability column with model.classes_ using the declared positive label, or model.classes_[1] when none is declared. Pass a binary indicator for that same label as y_true; roc_auc_score does not accept pos_label. Preserve the original labels for other metrics and record the positive-label convention. For roc_auc_ovr pass the full aligned probability matrix with labels=model.classes_, multi_class='ovr', average='macro'. When the evaluated partition lacks some model classes, never pass a column subset of the probability matrix to roc_auc_score with multi_class='ovr' (its rows no longer sum to 1); compute the macro value as the unweighted mean of binary roc_auc_score(y_true == c, proba[:, j]) over the classes present, and print the classes left out. Parsing, derived features, column selection and ordering needed later must be reproducible by the saved importable pipeline. Learned transforms fit only on the frozen training rows. Deterministic table preparation may precede the split only through a declared prepared-data artifact. Later steps pass the declared source feature schema to the saved pipeline, never assume derived columns already exist in a freshly loaded partition. Inspect fitted input names; do not invent missing columns or fit replacement preprocessing during evaluation.
[RL-0027] Before combining saved transformers, compare their feature_names_in_. Two saved objects that both expect the raw feature columns were fitted side by side, not in sequence; never chain one after the other, because the second then receives transformed output instead of the raw columns. Use only the one the step needs, normally the most complete, or place both side by side on the raw feature DataFrame (FeatureUnion). Chain an object after another only when its feature_names_in_ match the other's output names.
